story_log.title: Bills beat Rams 37-34 in OT thriller on MNF — Josh Allen finally wins overtime, Tyler Bass game-winner after Harrison Mevis blocked kick
story_log.development: Buffalo beat LA 37-34 in OT per ground truth — Josh Allen finally won his first career overtime game (was 0-7) per HaterReport/SportsCenter. Tyler Bass game-winning FG after Rams' Harrison Mevis 48-yarder blocked per SportsCenter/ClutchPoints. James Cook fumbled in OT, Aaron Donald recovered, Rams drove but kick blocked per HaterReport/ClutchPoints. Allen: 12-19, 331 TOT yards, 2 TOT TD, 121 rush yards (most since 2018), 1 INT per StatMuse/HaterReport. Stafford and Allen both threw for 300+, 4th quarter shootout per HaterReport/NFLMemes. Alaric Jackson threw punch at Bradley Chubb after game per HaterReport/ClutchPoints. Bills improve to 4-1, first in AFC East per ground truth. Rams fall to 2-3, 3rd in NFC West per ground truth.

lead_story.topic: Bills beat Rams 37-34 in OT thriller on MNF — Josh Allen finally wins overtime, Tyler Bass game-winner after Harrison Mevis blocked kick
lead_story.headline: Josh Allen finally breaks OT curse

tweets.text:
MONDAY NIGHT FOOTBALL INSTANT CLASSIC 🔥

BILLS WIN IT ON A FG IN OVERTIME ‼️

Josh Allen vs Rams:

210 PASS YDS
121 RUSH YDS (most since 2018)
2 TOT TD

His first ever OT win.

lead_story.research_notes: CONTINUING [Day 2]: Josh Allen was 0-7 in overtime games entering tonight — the longest active OT losing streak in the NFL. Tonight he finally won one, in the most Josh Allen way possible: 121 rush yards (most since 2018), a fumble by James Cook that let the Rams drive for a potential game-winner, and then a blocked kick that gave Buffalo one more chance. Tyler Bass nailed the game-winner. The game itself was an instant classic: Stafford and Allen both threw for 300+, the 4th quarter was a shootout, and the whole thing felt like a playoff game in October. Alaric Jackson threw a punch at Bradley Chubb after the game (caught on camera). Bills improve to 4-1, first in the AFC East. Rams fall to 2-3. Allen told SVP: 'I haven't been a fan of overtime games in my career, so we get the first one. We'll take it.' Now has 26% chance to win MVP per betting markets. Research the history of long OT losing streaks by star QBs — how many games did it take for others to finally win one? Name them. The 0-7 mark was a running joke all season; this ends it. Also: this was one of the best MNF games in years. Rank it against other instant-classic MNF games from the last decade. Where does it land? The Hailee Steinfeld angle: Bills are 1-0 at SoFi with her there, Rams are 0-3 with Madison Beer. That's a real stat people are tracking. Use it if you can land it without forcing it.

tweets.text: The Brewers are up 2-0 on the Dodgers. And they're doing what the Dodgers typically do: imposing their will and making their opponent play their game. Column, free at ESPN, on Milwaukee taking control of the NLCS: https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/50170393/playoffs-2026-brewers-dodgers-nlcs-game-2-milwaukee-new-level

supporting_stories.research_notes: CONTINUING [Day 3, TIER 1 ELIMINATION-ROUND GAME]: Milwaukee beat Los Angeles 7-4 to take a 2-0 series lead. William Contreras hit a 3-run HR in the 5th. Yoshinobu Yamamoto — who was lights-out in last year's postseason — got knocked out in the 3rd inning (2.2 IP, 3 ER), his shortest postseason start ever. Jake Bauers worked a 12-pitch walk to load the bases before Christian Yelich's 2-run single chased Yamamoto. The Dodgers are in rough shape: they haven't hit, they didn't win a Yamamoto start, and now they're down 2-0 heading home. Jeff Passan wrote a column: 'The Brewers are imposing their will and making the Dodgers play their game.' Research: how often does a defending World Series champion go down 2-0 in the LCS? What's their historical comeback rate? Also: the Dodgers are considering benching Shohei Ohtani for Game 3 (0 HR, 1 RBI since Aug 19). If they do that, it's a massive story. Monitor that closely. The Brewers' brand of baseball — relentless, menacing, mistake-free — is exactly what they were supposed to be. Name the other teams in recent history that played this way in October. Rank them.
